chapter_theme: A song at Konganagiri (கொங்கணகிரி): a litany of requests, for control of the senses, love in Tamil praise, knowledge from austerity and the way to release, a mind turned from women to Murugan, and worldly honour besides.

616.reading: The song is a string of prayers, each ending 'grant': a mind like Ganapati's that has driven off the five senses and a thought beyond night and day; a mind to praise Murugan with love in the Tamil that grows on earth; the knowledge of austerity, so that as a servant he gains release and a way to the moon-space; a grand palanquin and splendour esteemed in the eight directions; a mind that turns from the pleasure of women to think of Murugan; and the meaning that a father gained by grace on the southern bank in Kongu. It ends with Murugan, younger brother of the elephant-faced one, at Konganagiri.
616.nuance: A rare song with no confession and no myth, only petitions (அருள்வாயே eight times). It asks for both release (அடிமை முத்திபெற, சந்திர வெளிக்கு வழி, the moon-space of the yogi) and a palanquin with worldly honour (தண்டிகை கனப் பவுசு), without seeing a conflict. கொங்கில் உயிர் பெற்று வளர் தென்கரையில் அப்பர் அருள் may allude to a Kongu miracle of restoring life; I cannot identify it, and the மண்டலிகர் line is also unclear.

links.note: Among its petitions 616 asks for a thought beyond dusk and day (அந்தி பகல் அற்ற நினைவு) and a way to the moon-space (சந்திர வெளி). Tirumanthiram 1856 stays in the place where night and day are not (இராப்பகல் அற்ற இடத்தே) and drinks bliss at the Lord's feet. The shared phrase names the same state beyond the alternation of day and night, asked for in one and claimed in the other.
